simple.meaning: שֹׁעָר (shôʻâr) is a Hebrew object word meaning “harsh or horrid , i.e. offensive.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Jeremiah 29:17. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.

simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.full: H8182. shoar [ שֹׁעָר ] adjective horrid, disgusting (Ba NB 167 ); — plural הַשֹּׁעָרִיוֺ כַּתְּאֵנִיוֺ Jer 29:17 (uneatable).

occurrences.englishText: Yahweh of Armies says: “Behold, I will send on them the sword, the famine, and the pestilence, and will make them like rotten figs that can’t be eaten, they are so bad.
